judulDokumen: Perpindahan Kayan Uma' Lekan dari Apau Kayan ke Miau Baru (Part 1)

ringkasan.Jumlah ilustrasi: 13 ilustrasi Gemini + 1 adegan peta animasi (adegan 10, dengan prompt cadangan) + 2 lembar karakter (Amai Laway Ngau, Bo' Delinda')
ringkasan.Kadar dramatis: Terjaga (korban jiwa di sepanjang jalan; keturunan para perantau masih tinggal di Miau Baru)
ringkasan.Premis: Sebuah semboyan menyebut perpindahan seberat langit dan bumi; orang Kayan Uma' Lekan tetap memikulnya, dan kehilangan orang di hampir setiap pemondokan.
ringkasan.Adegan khusus: Adegan 10 = peta animasi (rute Apau Kayan ke Sungai Kelai). Datanya di bagian Peta animasi (kontrak v1.5); cadangan: ilustrasi dari prompt adegan 10
ringkasan.Asumsi: Durasi 2:30, kadar Terjaga, judul kerja, elemen merek dihitung 3,5 detik (kartu Ulikan saja)

Character reference sheet of Amai Laway Ngau.
Amai Laway Ngau, a Kayan Uma' Lekan elder and spokesman from the Apau Kayan highlands of Borneo in the early 1960s, a man in his late forties. Lean, sinewy build of an upriver farmer and boatman; warm medium-brown skin; long face with high cheekbones; narrow deep-set dark eyes; straight thick brows; broad flat nose; thin firm lips; faint lines at the eye corners; straight black hair cut short with a few grey strands; no tattoos; earlobes slightly stretched with no earrings. He wears a faded ivory-white long-sleeved cotton shirt with the sleeves rolled to the elbow, plain dark brown knee-length cotton shorts, and goes barefoot. A parang machete in a plain wooden sheath bound with split rattan hangs on a cord at his left hip. He leans slightly forward when he speaks, open palms raised, and listens with his head tilted.

Bo' Delinda', a Wehea Dayak elder leader from Muara Wahau, East Kalimantan, in 1963, a man of about sixty. Stocky, broad-shouldered build; deep brown weathered skin; round, broad face with heavy cheeks; heavy-lidded calm dark eyes; sparse grey brows; wide flat nose; full lips set in a straight line; deep lines from nose to mouth; close-cropped grey hair; earlobes unstretched. He wears a collarless long-sleeved cotton shirt dyed dark indigo, a plain dark brown cotton sarong wrapped at the waist and falling to mid-calf, a narrow plain dark cloth headband tied at the back, and goes barefoot. A small woven rattan shoulder bag hangs at his right side. He sits very still with both hands resting on his knees, speaks slowly, and looks steadily at the person in front of him.

caption.caption:
Tahun 1964, 852 orang Kayan meninggalkan kampung mereka di jantung Kalimantan.
Kayan Uma' Lekan dari Long Hiban dan Long Belerang di Apau Kayan berjalan menuju Sungai Wahau, setelah sumpah adat diikat dengan orang Wehea di Muara Wahau. Part 1 mengikuti mereka sampai Sungai Kelai.
Pernahkah keluargamu punya kisah pindah kampung? Ceritakan di komentar.
Dituturkan ulang dari sumber sejarah; ilustrasi adalah rekonstruksi. Sumber utama: Purba dkk., BPNB Pontianak (2012). Sebagian kisah bersumber dari semboyan turun-temurun Kayan. Part 1 dari 2.

batas.sumber: Konvensi Batas Inggris–Belanda 20 Juni 1891 dan Konvensi Den Haag 1928

catatan: Pemicu `pemondokan` memakai kemunculan pertamanya di narasi ("membangun pemondokan").

Semua titik berstatus perkiraan karena S1 tidak memberi koordinat pemondokan; peta menampilkan catatan "rute perkiraan". Titik awal di hulu Sungai Kayan sekitar Apau Kayan (S8), titik akhir di hulu Sungai Kelai.
Long Penawan sengaja tidak diberi label karena letaknya tidak tercatat. Pondok pertama di rute mewakili pemondokan pertama itu; kalimat Long Penawan diucapkan saat rute sudah utuh.
Batas Kalimantan–Sarawak sudah berlaku pada 1964–1965 (Konvensi 1891, berlaku 11 Agustus 1892; sektor kecil di Sarawak disempurnakan 1928). Sumber: S19 (A) dan S20 (D).
